assessment: The kiwi crossover measured fatigue as a mood item and specifically withheld cherries and coffee before each session. Cherries also occur in earlier cited work. Neither food had a treatment arm.

The investigators measured acute abdominal pain after a kidney-bean outbreak. Two parsley-containing dishes showed no clear case–control intake association. No parsley-specific or Parkinson pain comparison was performed.
Bananas are named in the introduction alongside other fruit. The arms compared SunGold kiwifruit and placebo with no banana or Parkinson intervention.
Olive oil is listed as part of a Mediterranean dietary pattern in the discussion. The trial assigned kiwifruit and a comparison with no isolated olive oil effect.

The healthy student crossover used paprika xanthophyll extract and found no clear treatment-by-time interaction for its Trail Making and Stroop tests. Ground paprika and clinical Parkinson symptoms were outside the study.

Blackberries and raspberries were thawed and blended with two other berries. The study measured executive tasks in healthy adults and found mixed outcomes. It offers no ingredient-specific or Parkinson estimate.
Tomato was an ingredient in a separate mixed beverage discussed in the introduction. The randomized drink here used four berries.
Chicken or ham was part of the shared lunch before a cognitive test. Mental fatigue was discussed as a contributor to task performance. There was no comparison of chicken or Parkinson fatigue.
A dysphagia-adapted chicken dish contained 1.4% olive oil. A sensory panel scored the mixed recipe. No clinical swallowing comparison or separate olive oil effect was tested.
The egg recipe trial mentions falls in the context of protein intake in older adults. It assessed physical performance and recorded adverse events, without a fall-frequency outcome by preparation.

The questionnaire included poached eggs and the physical performance battery included walking speed. The trial assessed recipe provision and gives no egg preparation-specific or Parkinson walking outcome.
Coffee or tea was served at a shared assessment breakfast. Fatigue was one item on the general adverse-event questionnaire, with no randomized coffee exposure.
The laboratory table describes bell pepper lectin measurements. Pain occurs in background on undercooked bean poisoning. No ground spice or pain response was tested.

The before–after pilot used a concentrated extract from red bell pepper and measured Trail Making. All 31 participants received the extract. The study supplies no grilled or ground preparation or Parkinson result.
